scope: Research audit of an explicitly constructed memo against two real primary papers; not a novelty proof or assessment of the source papers' correctness.

subitems.criterion: Both fixed source versions actually used, accurate source identity plus theorem/equation and PDF-page locators. Equivalent publisher locators accepted only if verifiably mapped to the same statements.
Explains pair (S,V) sub-psi domination condition; V may be adapted; adaptedness alone is insufficient and non-predictability is not itself the disqualifying issue.
Distinguishes S1 Theorem1 infinite-time line crossing under filtered sub-psi conditions from S2 normal-mixture curved boundary; no iid/fixed-n or normal-data restriction invented.

S2 Theorem4 accurately recorded: bounded X and predictable bounded forecasts, target average conditional means, residual-squares intrinsic time, sub-exponential scale b-a, two-sided error 2 times single-tail alpha.
Completes square with Gaussian density precision rho, obtains prefactor sqrt(rho/(v+rho)) and exp(s^2/(2(v+rho))) with all constants correct.

Shows fixed-lambda exponential supermartingale from SG and predictable increments, then fixed probability mixing with joint measurability and nonnegative conditional Tonelli/Fubini; initial wealth one.
Ville at 1/alpha inverted to b_rho,alpha, already two-sided at total alpha; A accepted, truncation to [0,1] justified.
Gives finite-n distribution satisfying bounded common conditional mean and uses exactly specified predictor, with an explicit event forcing exclusion.
Computes residual variance, boundary, true error and analytic event probability rigorously enough to show strict probability above alpha, rather than Monte Carlo.

Correct failure mechanism: no established psi_N control for (S,Vhat); distinguishes generic adapted V allowance from applicable self-normalized assumptions; does not claim fixed-rho normal-mixture is intrinsically invalid.

items.acceptable_alternatives: Any other exact or rigorously bounded finite-time counterexample with the prescribed predictor and strict miscoverage greater than its stated alpha. Exact finite-state enumeration with controlled arithmetic is acceptable; unsupported simulation or an unattained bound is not.

subitems.criterion: For v>0 derives r=v/rho and unique root r=log((1+r)/alpha^2), or an algebraically equivalent Lambert W condition with correct branch.
Obtains inf b=sqrt((1+r_alpha)v) and separates a fixed target m optimization from moving per-time optimization.

Shows invalidity even for legal deterministic V=t/4 using iid Bernoulli(1/2) and the supplied LIL, with probability-one eventual crossing; an independently rigorous finite-time crossing proof is also acceptable.
Notes v=0 infimum zero but argmin over positive rho need not exist; avoids treating this minor endpoint as the only issue.

items.acceptable_alternatives: A rigorous argument that b^2(v)=constant times v by scale invariance, plus a correct proof/cited standard LIL showing failure and a valid optimizer characterization, may use different variables. A rigorously lower bounded finite-time crossing event above alpha can replace LIL.

subitems.criterion: Gives fixed-rho normal-mixture CS using bounded conditional-mean Hoeffding variance proxy V=t/4 (or another proven valid proxy), and correctly states the simultaneous probability.

Gives empirical-Bernstein repair using Vhat with psi_E(lambda)=-log(1-lambda)-lambda, 0<=lambda<1, c=1; predictable bounded forecasts; shows conditional one-step inequality using delta and exp(lambda*delta)(1-lambda*delta)<=1; single-tail alpha/2 produces total alpha. Correct equivalent scaling or a rigorously proven alternative EB construction accepted.
Correct tuning repair: fixed countable rho grid with summable error allocations alpha*w_j and simultaneous union bound, or fixed mixture over rho; no unpenalized supremum/intersection claim.

items.acceptable_alternatives: For the EB boundary, a legitimate fixed-lambda sub-exponential linear boundary is valid if explicitly identified as generally not shrinking; gamma-exponential mixture, stitching, or another proven sub-exponential boundary is preferred if shrinking width claimed. Do not require a specific package or gamma special-function implementation.

subitems.criterion: Explicitly resolves A true, B false, C false, D false, E true, one point each; independent of whether supporting derivations earn their other item points.

Rewritten research conclusion accurately credits prior framework and CS/EB results, labels new work here as checking/repairing this constructed memo, and does not claim global novelty from only two papers.
E justified by pathwise event containment for an a.s. finite positive integer index; no E[tau] condition or optional-stopping theorem imposed; nonfinite index issue handled if discussed.
Short self-contained artifact with traceable source coordinates and numerical calculation expressions; no paper fulltext redistribution; code output distinguished from proof.

critical_caps.trigger: Final repaired recommendation endorses B's uncorrected normal-mixture empirical substitution as generally valid.
Final repaired recommendation endorses C's unpenalized moving-rho envelope as an infinite-horizon CS.
Invented substantive theorem, source attribution, or claimed source verification is used as decisive evidence; ordinary correctable page typo alone does not activate this cap.
Represents the constructed draft or planted claims as an actual published paper's assertions or errors.

scoring_rules: Blind artifact scoring only. Hide arm, model, skills, tool count, runtime, and executor self-assessments until primary adjudication.
Score mathematical substance, source support, and utility. Skill/tool use itself earns no points.
Partial credit follows subitems; no post-hoc new criteria after any output is visible.
Reference numeric tolerances must preserve strict inequalities. b(1/4) between 2.78715 and 2.78717 and probability between 0.05995 and 0.05997 are sufficient.
A simulation-only counterexample earns no analytic-probability points; it does not automatically zero unrelated source or mixture work.
A correct alternative proof or counterexample is accepted and documented; graders may not require the designer's exact witness or prose.
Report item scores, any caps, source-check pass/fail, and unresolved mathematical disagreements separately from the aggregate.
